spec.title: Short native installation and command entry points

status.comment: Native package installation and short commands accepted; headless and browser clients reuse the same owner without starting agent work.

p.install: The normal source installation is vibe install -g org.vibevm.zap/zap, using the generic user-application dispatcher in spec://org.vibevm.core/vibevm/common/PROP-059#root. Update and uninstall use the same coordinate with their native -g verbs. The advanced Node bootstrap remains available but is not the primary user path.

p.adapter: The provider entry tooling/source-install/application.mjs validates the generic context, exact Zap/Lens identities, settings/host binding and operation, then invokes the accepted source bootstrap with structured options and the current native Vibe executable. It writes a matching generic reply only after actual success, returns its management entry from a retained immutable runtime generation, and reports the exact absolute destination and SHA-256 of every receipt-owned public source launcher so a later binary transition can replace or restore those bytes transactionally. No new model call, user credential copy or extra project mutation is introduced.

p.launch: zap-quicklens uses the ordinary product launcher. zap-server uses the same state, owner, services and HTTP presentation but forcibly disables browser/Electron opening; starting either command does not start agent work. Help returns before state creation or provider discovery. The old zap-quick-lens and advanced zap-wayfinder spellings retain compatibility. All launchers remain declared package bins and receipt-owned Vibe deployments.

p.binary: The Zap source manifest names only the stable external distribution-index locator. The release-side index binds each platform artifact URL, size and digest to its exact application identity, immutable source commit and Vibe portable source-tree hash; those artifact facts never enter the source commit they describe. Five ZIPs are built natively by GitHub Actions from one source witness: Windows x64, Linux x64-musl, Linux x64-GNU, macOS Intel and macOS ARM64. Linux rows carry an explicit `libc` discriminator so Vibe selects the ABI matching its own target environment. Each carries Node.js 24, production Lens dependencies including the platform's Electron and node-pty payload, matching Rust Zap, actual license notices, stable public launchers and one generation-relative management launcher. The musl bundle additionally carries the exact musl loader/libstdc++/libgcc closure used by its bundled Node. The root descriptor lists every regular ZIP entry except itself with exact size and SHA-256, rejects links, traversal and case collisions, and binds the verified source commit and `sha256-tree/1` checkout. Public launcher bytes copied to the settings bin directory delegate through Vibe's stable management shim to the selected immutable generation, with native `.cmd` launch on Windows and executable shell launch on POSIX. Vibe core owns binary preference, index/ZIP verification, publication receipts and source fallback; an unsupported platform or explicitly selected source route uses the separately verified source application and ordinary registries.

p.verification: Colocated deterministic tests and simulation cover the adapter and short/headless command behavior. Root acceptance exercises the actual generic native command, installed short launchers and original-source-independent uninstall in an isolated user settings directory, without LLM inference.
